patterns.what_worked: The sweep's item rows named the live consumer for each widget, so every build was 'find the consumer, then write the widget against it' rather than guesswork. Re-reading the tree before each edit caught that P-22's range widget had ALREADY shipped and only the default was missing - building a second widget would have been a duplicate. Driving the badge widget against the REAL practice_ui module (injected into the options sandbox) proved the whole chain - widget -> module entry point -> class table - instead of a copy of the logic. Mutation proofs on a /tmp/opencode copy (11/11 killed, each restored byte-identical) caught that the Flame Shock flip silently killed the guide icon's countdown swipe; the pins now say 'refresh on expiry' and a separate case proves the explicit override still rides the swipe.
patterns.what_was_hard: Three of the four items were not 'add a widget' in the simple sense: P-22's widget existed (only the default was owed), the Forever Rend widget's provider read lives in a class file this lane may not touch, and the Flame Shock flip changes visible guide behaviour (a live dot is no longer re-applied, so the slot's swipe never rides). Each needed a documented default-off state and a filed follow-up rather than an invented value. The shaman lane was editing classes/shaman.lua and tests/shaman_guide_state.lua LIVE through the whole run, so the harness was read twice and the mutation baseline had to be re-taken after it landed.
patterns.skill_gap: I nearly shipped the Forever Rend widget as if it were live. The house rule in this very suite says an unread key must not get a widget - the honest resolution was to ship the key + widget + off default as the spec asked, cite the engine consumer, and pin the missing provider link explicitly (with the exact one-line shape) so the gap is visible rather than silent.

HU-9's row is answered - the widget landed on the Progress page - and the operator closes it.
